Response: New legislation introduced in the 93rd Congress in the form of HR 4758 does not include such an exemption.
<u>Comment</u>: Kentucky suggests that the Secretary of the Interior have sole jurisdiction for endangered species.
Response: The point is relevant to the proposed legislation rather than the Environmental Statement. However, our comment appropriate to this question may be found in our reply to the Florida Department of Administration, Bureau of State Planning and Development Clearinghouse.
Comment: The Department of Fish and Wildlife Resources suggests establishment of an outside review board to determine whether a Federal agency's policies or program jeopardize the continued existence of endangered species. Response: While we agree with Kentucky's comment, we believe such a review board to be unnecessary at this point if all safe-guards provided by the law are effectively utilized. There will, of course, be a constant change of public decisions to be made regarding the effect of economic development projects on the natural environment. Most of these projects will have an environmental effect and will threaten wildlife but possibly without threatening existence of the species. The proposed legislation is designed and intended to provide the means for the decision as to whether the species is threatened. Implementation of the proposal will satisfy the same purpose for which a review board might be appointed.
